hints.title: Index-Parity Node Reordering Obstacle
hints.text: Splitting by node values rather than node indices produces incorrect arrangements. How can interleaving two reference chains allow you to regroup odd and even indexed nodes in a single pass?

hints.title: Odd and Even Splicing Invariant
hints.text: Maintain separate odd and even pointers, alternating link advances while preserving the even chain head to attach at the end of the odd chain.

hints.title: Dual-Chain Interleaving Procedure
hints.text: If head is null, return head. Set odd to head and even to head.next, saving evenHead as even. While even and even.next exist: set odd.next to even.next, advance odd, set even.next to odd.next, and advance even. Finally, link odd.next to evenHead. Return head.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def oddEvenList(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        if not head or not head.next:
            return head
        odd = head
        even = head.next
        even_head = even
        while even and even.next:
            odd.next = even.next
            odd = odd.next
            even.next = odd.next
            even = even.next
        odd.next = even_head
        return head
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (0 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Single pass grouping odd and even indices in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Allocating two new node arrays violates the constant extra space requirement.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct in-place pointer leapfrogging runs in linear time with zero extra heap allocations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Preserving the original relative order among odd nodes and among even nodes.
